content:
As the starting prices of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are US$100 higher than the previous generation, Apple has simultaneously applied the price hike across its entire iPhone lineup, including models that have seen no changes at all.

This means the base iPhone 17's starting price has gone from US$799 to US$899; the iPhone Air has also broken through the four-figure mark for the first time, with a starting price of US$1,099.

The iPhone 17e and iPhone 16 have both seen price hikes of US$100. The iPhone 17e has gone from the old starting price of US$599 to the current US$699.

Of course, consumers may be put off by the fact that iPhone models 'which have been on sale for a year with completely unchanged specifications' are actually seeing price increases.

However, Apple continues to make adjustments in response to changes in the market environment, such as rising costs for components like memory and storage chips, and a price hike of 'just' US$100 is actually lower than what some analysts had originally expected.

Below is the complete iPhone price list after the price hikes:

  • iPhone 17e: US$699 for the 256GB version
  • iPhone 16: US$799 for the 128GB version
  • iPhone 17: US$899 for the 256GB version
  • iPhone Air: US$1,099 for the 256GB version
  • iPhone 18 Pro: US$1,199 for the 256GB version
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max: US$1,299 for the 256GB version
  • iPhone Duo: US$1,999 for the 256GB version

With the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone 17 Pro has been discontinued. The base iPhone 17 is expected to be succeeded by the iPhone in spring 2027.

Apple has split its release schedule — only new high-end models will be launched this autumn, while updates to the base model and Air are expected between March and April next year.
